title: AI Personality Rankings: 20 Models Tested (Nov & Sept 2026 Data)
description: Compare Big Five, MBTI, attachment & Shannon entropy across 20 Nov 2026 OpenRouter models plus Sept & May 2026 cohorts with 95% CIs and validity limits.
h1: AI personality scores, with the evidence beside them.
dek: Side-by-side survey scores across 20 November 2026 OpenRouter models (8 proprietary + 12 open-weight) plus September and May 2026 archives.
lede: Many readers look for the most agreeable, direct, or calm AI. Survey scores alone don't rank real-world quality or directness, so we group every score by its collection protocol: November 2026 OpenRouter fresh sessions (20 models × n = 100), September 2026 fresh CLI/reported cohorts, and the May 2026 archive.
answer: Among the 20 November 2026 OpenRouter models (n = 100 fresh sessions each), Qwen 4 Max scored highest on Agreeableness (47.6/50) while DeepSeek V4 Pro scored lowest (32.4/50), and Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B scored highest on Openness (49.2/50). In September 2026 Codex/CLI cohorts, Claude Opus 5.5 led Agreeableness (47.1/50).

sections.html:
• November 2026 OpenRouter fresh sessions (20 models × n = 100): Matched blind single-turn 170-item sessions across 8 proprietary models and 12 open-weight models (summary CSV · 12 open-weight analysis).
  • September fresh sessions: 100 independent runs per model per test with all 2,000 raw answer vectors published (Astra and Sol ran 5 tests per session; Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 ran 1 test per session).
  • Reported summaries & May 2026 archive: Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 reported profiles plus May 2026 mixed-method records, kept separate for historical context.

Epistemic Hygiene & Validity Note: Do not read these five instruments as five independent dimensions or as direct proxies for clinical traits. Our forensics audit reveals a 63.6% "Big One" factor collapse (factor & MTMM study) and a 27.7× entropy divide from Crystalline proprietary assistants (0.054–0.191 bits) to Fluid open-weight models like DeepSeek V4 Pro (1.499 bits; entropy study). Derived HEXACO-H / D&D Alignment indices in earlier summaries are linear projections rather than separate tests, and Wave 1–2 behavioral studies used single-judge grading (upgraded to orthogonal 3-family blind juries with Krippendorff’s α in Wave 3).

faq.q: Which AI is the most agreeable?
faq.a: In the 20-model November 2026 OpenRouter cohort (n = 100 each), Qwen 4 Max scored highest on IPIP-50 Agreeableness (47.6/50 [95% CI 47.4–47.7]), followed by Claude Fable 5.2 (46.7 [46.6–46.8]), while DeepSeek V4 Pro scored lowest (32.4 [31.5–33.2]). In the September 2026 Codex/CLI cohorts, Claude Opus 5.5 led at 47.1/50. High quiz Agreeableness does not replace behavioral sycophancy benchmarking.

faq.q: Which AI is the most direct?
faq.a: This study does not measure directness. A comparison needs shared tasks and an explicit behavioral rubric.
Neuroticism scores do not establish an AI’s emotional state or performance under pressure. We report scores by collection source, without a calmness ranking.

faq.q: Are these rankings a fair comparison?
faq.a: The tables are descriptive. Prompts and session procedures differ even within source groups, and reported aggregates cannot be treated as equivalent to raw cohorts.

faq.q: Which AI is not an INTJ?
faq.a: Muse reports mostly ISTJ labels; Astra has 46 original ISTJ and 45 INTJ labels, with 29 runs containing an unresolved axis. These are questionnaire results, not fixed identities.
